verses.text: After Ehud died, the Israelites again did evil in the LORD's eyes.
So the LORD sold them to Jabin, a king of Canaan who ruled in Hazor. The commander of his army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth Haggoyim.
Sisera had nine hundred iron chariots, and he cruelly crushed the Israelites for twenty years. So they cried out to the LORD for help.
At that time Deborah, a prophet and the wife of Lappidoth, was leading Israel as judge.
She used to sit under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites came to her to settle their disputes.

She sent for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali and said to him, "The LORD, the God of Israel, commands you: 'Go and gather ten thousand men from the tribes of Naphtali and Zebulun, and lead them up to Mount Tabor.
I will lure Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, with his chariots and his soldiers, to the Kishon River, and I will give him into your hands.'"
Barak said to her, "If you go with me, I will go. But if you do not go with me, I will not go."
Deborah said, "Very well, I will go with you. But you will not get the honour for this journey, because the LORD will hand Sisera over to a woman." So Deborah went with Barak to Kedesh.
Barak called Zebulun and Naphtali together at Kedesh. Ten thousand men followed him, and Deborah also went with him.
Now Heber the Kenite had left the other Kenites, the descendants of Hobab, Moses' brother-in-law. He had set up his tent near the big tree at Zaanannim, near Kedesh.
Sisera was told that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.
So Sisera called out all his nine hundred iron chariots and all his soldiers, from Harosheth Haggoyim to the Kishon River.
Then Deborah said to Barak, "Go! This is the day the LORD has given Sisera into your hands. The LORD has gone ahead of you!" So Barak went down Mount Tabor with ten thousand men behind him.
As Barak advanced, the LORD threw Sisera and all his chariots and army into panic before Barak's swords. Sisera jumped down from his chariot and ran away on foot.
Barak chased the chariots and the army as far as Harosheth Haggoyim. All of Sisera's soldiers were killed with the sword. Not one was left.
But Sisera ran away on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, because there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and Heber's family.
Jael went out to meet Sisera and said to him, "Come in, my lord, come right in. Do not be afraid." So he went into her tent, and she covered him with a blanket.
He said, "Please give me some water. I am thirsty." She opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him up again.
He told her, "Stand at the entrance of the tent. If anyone comes and asks you, 'Is anyone here?' say 'No.'"
But Jael, Heber's wife, picked up a tent peg and a hammer and quietly went to him while he lay fast asleep, worn out. She drove the peg through his head into the ground, and he died.

Just then Barak came by, chasing Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. "Come," she said, "I will show you the man you are looking for." So he went in with her, and there lay Sisera, dead, with the tent peg through his head.
On that day God defeated Jabin, the Canaanite king, in front of the Israelites.
And the Israelites grew stronger and stronger against Jabin king of Canaan until they destroyed him.
